Short answer: In modern unified-memory GPUs, decoding latency is no longer limited by compute; it’s limited by how fast you can move tokens between LPDDR5X system memory, the GPU’s L2 cache, and the on-chip L1/shared memory where the attention kernels run. Hybrid linear-attention (HQA) and full-attention (FA) models expose different memory access patterns, so they hit different bottlenecks. Below is a concrete, quantitative breakdown.

Here’s a self-contained Python implementation of a bounded lock-free-style ring buffer simulator with producer/consumer backpressure metrics and unit tests.

Notes:
- “Lock-free style” here means:
  - Single-producer / single-consumer (SPSC) to keep it simple and correct without complex CAS loops.
  - Uses a single atomic head/tail with modulo indexing.
  - No Python-level locks; concurrency is simulated via threads.
